data.stem: In the Indian parliamentary system, who is described as the de facto executive?
data.explanation: The Prime Minister is correct: real executive power rests with the Prime Minister and council, whereas the President is the nominal de jure head of State. The Chief Justice and the Speaker are not executive heads, so the other options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Article provides that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President?
data.explanation: Article 75 is correct. Article 74 deals with the council aiding and advising the President, Article 77 with conduct of government business and Article 78 with the Prime Minister's duty to inform the President, so those are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The Prime Minister's duty to furnish information to the President is laid down in which Article?
data.explanation: Article 78 is correct as it lists the Prime Minister's duties towards the President. Article 74 is about the council's advice, Article 75 about appointment and responsibility, and Article 88 about ministers' rights in the Houses, so they are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who was the first President to use personal discretion in appointing a Prime Minister, by naming Charan Singh in 1979?
data.explanation: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy is correct; he named Charan Singh after the Janata government under Morarji Desai fell. Zail Singh used his judgement later, in 1984, and Giri and Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed did not make this choice, so the others are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Whom did President Zail Singh appoint as Prime Minister after the assassination of Indira Gandhi in 1984?
data.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi is correct; the President set aside the caretaker precedent. Gulzari Lal Nanda had acted as Prime Minister after Nehru and Shastri, not in 1984, while Charan Singh was named in 1979 and Rao took office in 1991, so those are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of the Prime Minister:
1. The Constitution lays down a detailed procedure for selecting the Prime Minister.
2. In a hung Lok Sabha the President may exercise personal discretion.
3. The Prime Minister must always be a member of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
data.explanation: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong because Article 75 says merely that the President appoints. Statement 3 is wrong because the Prime Minister can sit in the Rajya Sabha or be a non-member for six months.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which one of the following statements about the 1996 Supreme Court ruling on Prime Ministers is correct?
options: A non-member of Parliament cannot be appointed at all
A non-member may serve for one year before joining Parliament
A non-member may be appointed but must join a House within six months
Only a Lok Sabha member can be appointed
data.explanation: A non-member may be appointed but must join a House within six months; otherwise the person ceases to be Prime Minister. The other options are incorrect, as the ruling set a six-month limit and allowed either House.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following Prime Ministers was NOT a Rajya Sabha member at the time of taking office?
data.explanation: Narasimha Rao is correct: he was not a Rajya Sabha member when he became Prime Minister in 1991. Indira Gandhi (1966), Deve Gowda (1996) and Manmohan Singh (2004) are the three Prime Ministers named as Rajya Sabha members, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In which year did the Delhi High Court hold that a person need not prove a Lok Sabha majority before being appointed Prime Minister?
data.explanation: 1980 is correct. The Delhi High Court said the President may appoint first and ask for proof within a reasonable time. 1979 saw Charan Singh named, 1989 V. P. Singh took office, and 1996 was the Supreme Court ruling on non-members, so those years are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The Prime Minister holds office:
options: during the pleasure of the President
for a fixed term of five years
during the pleasure of the Speaker
data.explanation: The Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President, though in practice this means as long as the Lok Sabha's confidence lasts. There is no fixed term, age limit or role for the Speaker, so the other options are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The resignation of the Prime Minister dissolves the council of ministers.
2. The death of any other minister dissolves the council of ministers.
3. The Prime Minister can advise the President to dismiss a minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 3 only is correct. The Prime Minister's resignation or death ends the council. Statement 2 is wrong because the exit of another minister merely creates a vacancy that the Prime Minister may or may not fill.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following is NOT a chairmanship held by the Prime Minister?
data.explanation: The UPSC is not chaired by the Prime Minister; its chairman is appointed on the Prime Minister's advice and is an independent officer. NITI Aayog, the Inter-State Council and the National Integration Council are chaired by the Prime Minister, so the others are wrong choices.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who was the first non-Congress Prime Minister of India, having earlier been Chief Minister of Bombay State?
data.explanation: Morarji Desai is correct; he took office in March 1977. Charan Singh followed him as a former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, V. P. Singh led the National Front in 1989, and Chandrasekhar was never a Chief Minister, so the others are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Prime Minister was earlier Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh and was the first from South India?
data.explanation: P. V. Narasimha Rao is correct; he was Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 1971–73 and Prime Minister from 1991 to 1996. Deve Gowda led Karnataka, Gujral was never a Chief Minister, and Manmohan Singh was not one either, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Prime Minister was Chief Minister of Gujarat before taking office in May 2014?
data.explanation: Narendra Modi is correct; he was Chief Minister of Gujarat four times between 2001 and 2014. Vajpayee, Chandrasekhar and Gujral were not Chief Ministers, so those options are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Dr B. R. Ambedkar said that the functionary comparable to the US President under the Indian Constitution is:
options: the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
data.explanation: The Prime Minister is correct, since real executive power sits with that office. The President of the Union is a nominal head, whereas the Chief Justice and the Speaker are not executive heads at all, so those answers are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister and the President:
1. The Prime Minister advises the President on the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General.
2. The Prime Minister can recommend dissolution of the Lok Sabha at any time.
3. The President can appoint any person as a minister without the Prime Minister's recommendation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the President can appoint as ministers only persons the Prime Minister recommends, so options including it are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following describes the Prime Minister as 'a moon among lesser stars'?
data.explanation: Harcourt is correct. Morley used 'first among equals' and 'keystone of the cabinet arch', Laski called the Prime Minister central to the cabinet's formation, life and death, and Jennings compared the office to a sun, so the others are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following is true of a caretaker government in India?
options: The Constitution lays down its powers in a separate Part
It may freely launch major new policies
It is a convention for routine business, not a constitutional provision
It is appointed by the Chief Justice
data.explanation: It is a convention for routine business, not a constitutional provision. The Constitution has no caretaker clause, so the first option is wrong; it is not expected to launch major new policies, and the Chief Justice has no role in forming it.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which committee recommended that a caretaker government should not grant allowances, loans or salary increases or start new projects?
data.explanation: The Tarkunde Committee of 1974–75 is correct; it was an unofficial committee on electoral reforms set up under Jayaprakash Narayan. The Sarkaria, Punchhi and Rajamannar bodies dealt with Centre-State relations, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The dissolution of the Lok Sabha and the continuance of the outgoing ministry until elections are completed is best described as:
data.explanation: A caretaker arrangement is correct, as the outgoing ministry only handles routine business until a new one takes charge. An emergency is a separate constitutional power, a no-confidence vote removes a government, and a hung house means no clear majority, so those are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Arrange these Prime Ministers in the order in which they were appointed:
1. Charan Singh
2. P. V. Narasimha Rao
3. V. P. Singh
4. Deve Gowda
data.explanation: 1, 3, 2, 4 is correct: Charan Singh (1979), V. P. Singh (1989), Narasimha Rao (1991) and Deve Gowda (1996). The other orders place these dates wrongly, so they are incorrect.
data.label: practice
